root_cause.text: In hid-pidff's `pidff_init_fields()`, the condition-effect capability clearing used short-circuit `||` with `test_and_clear_bit()` on `dev->ffbit`, so only the first set conditional force-feedback bit was cleared and the remaining unsupported bits stayed advertised, leading to later NULL dereferences when those uninitialized effect fields were used.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces `if (test_and_clear_bit(FF_SPRING, ...) || ... || test_and_clear_bit(FF_INERTIA, ...))` with separate `test |= test_and_clear_bit(...)` calls for all four bits before checking `if (test)`, and the CVE/commit message explicitly says "NULL pointer dereferences were happening because not all the conditional effects bits were cleared."

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch replaces `if (test_and_clear_bit(FF_SPRING, ...) || ... || test_and_clear_bit(FF_INERTIA, ...))` with separate `test |= test_and_clear_bit(...)` calls for all four bits before checking `if (test)`, and the CVE/commit message explicitly says "NULL pointer dereferences were happening because not all the conditional effects bits were cleared."

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix condition-effect capability cleanup so all relevant FF bits are cleared before warning about an unknown condition effect layout.
intent_record.what: Within the PIDFF_FIND_FIELDS(set_condition, PID_SET_CONDITION, 1) block, the chained conditional using four test_and_clear_bit() calls combined with logical OR was replaced by a local bool variable initialized to false, updated with bitwise-OR assignment from each individual test_and_clear_bit() call, and then checked in a separate if (test) before emitting the warning.
intent_record.how: This ensures all four condition-effect capability bits (FF_SPRING, FF_DAMPER, FF_FRICTION, FF_INERTIA) are always tested and cleared instead of stopping after the first true result due to short-circuit evaluation, while still warning if any of them were present.

grouping_result.intent: Fix condition-effect capability cleanup so all relevant FF bits are cleared before warning about an unknown condition effect layout.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly fixes the root cause: replacing the short-circuit condition-effect FF bit clearing logic so all advertised unsupported bits are cleared, preventing later use of uninitialized effect fields and resulting NULL dereferences.

candidates.rationale: This starts the short-circuit OR chain. Because test_and_clear_bit() has side effects, using || means evaluation stops after the first set bit is cleared, leaving other unsupported condition-effect bits still advertised.
As part of the short-circuit OR chain, this side-effecting call may never execute if an earlier bit was set, contributing to unsupported FF bits remaining uncleared.
This side-effecting bit clear is guarded by prior || terms, so it can be skipped, leaving FRiction capability advertised even though the fields were not initialized.

This final side-effecting clear is part of the same faulty short-circuit expression and may not run, leaving unsupported inertia capability set and later causing dereference of uninitialized effect fields.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement begins the short-circuit || chain of side-effecting test_and_clear_bit() calls. Because || stops evaluation after the first true term, only the first advertised condition-effect capability may be cleared, leaving other unsupported bits set and later enabling use of uninitialized effect fields.
This side-effecting clear participates in the faulty short-circuit expression and may not execute if an earlier bit was set, leaving FF_DAMPER incorrectly advertised.
This side-effecting clear is also skipped when a prior || operand evaluates true, so FF_FRICTION can remain set even though its fields were not initialized.
This final operand is part of the same vulnerable short-circuit chain and may never run, leaving FF_INERTIA advertised and contributing to later NULL dereferences from uninitialized effect fields.
